title: Deep-time distances: dinosaurs vs the last total solar eclipse (million years)
time_coverage: 230 million years ago to 600 million years in the future

source.name: Orbital dynamics modeling of lunar recession and eclipse geometry

notes: The 600-million-year horizon for the last possible total solar eclipse is a widely cited estimate among researchers modeling the Moon's 3.8 cm/year recession (reported by AGU's Eos and multiple science outlets). The dinosaur-era dates (first dinosaurs ~230 million years ago in the Triassic; non-avian dinosaur extinction 66 million years ago via the Chicxulub impact) are well-established paleontological benchmarks used here for scale comparison, not derived from the eclipse study itself.
